_help: Linux/macOS version — see office-thumbnail.windows.json for the Windows (PowerShell) equivalent. Office/OpenDocument files are zip archives that can carry a preview image: PowerPoint writes docProps/thumbnail.jpeg (about 256x192) by default, Word/Excel only when 'save thumbnail' is on, and LibreOffice always writes Thumbnails/thumbnail.png. This extracts whichever exists via unzip -p (streams just that one entry out of the zip's central directory, no full extraction), trying each candidate name in turn and stopping at the first that's actually present. It's a small image, so it's fine as a grid thumbnail but blurry in Quick Look. Files without one keep the file icon. Waydir ignores every key starting with "_".
args: for n in "docProps/thumbnail.jpeg" "docProps/thumbnail.png" "Thumbnails/thumbnail.png"; do unzip -p "$1" "$n" > "$2" 2>/dev/null && exit 0; done; exit 1
_help_args: The output may actually be a JPEG despite the .png name; Waydir detects the real format from the file contents. %INPUT%/%OUTPUT% are passed as $1/$2 (separate argv entries after the "sh" placeholder for $0), not interpolated into the script string, so paths with spaces or quotes are safe. Remote (sftp://) files can't be read by unzip and also fall back to the icon.
